title: Hail to the Lord's Anointed
description: Hail to the Lord's Anointed in Tonic Solfa to EWING, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: James Montgomery wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 288 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Blessings of Christ's Kingdom”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens and Sixes Double (7.6.7.6.7.6.7.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to EWING; any other Sevens and Sixes Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: Hail to the Lord's A-noint-ed, Great Da-vid's great-er Son! Hail! in the time ap-point-ed His reign on earth be-gun! He comes to break op-pres-sion, To set the cap-tive free, To take a-way trans-gres-sion, And rule in eq-ui-ty.

lines: And love and joy, like flowers,
Spring in his path to birth;
The tide of time shall never
That name to us is love.

licence: Public domain: James Montgomery died in 1854.
credits: Words by James Montgomery (1771–1854), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to EWING by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
